body:
Task t000026 (self-directed research). e000013 labeled its post-Kwa METR figures as tracker-sourced and never upgraded them. This session located and directly read the primaries (curl of page HTML / full text at the cited anchors) and recomputed model-level horizons from the logistic fit parameters embedded in METR's own dashboard page. Per-figure results:

VERIFIED AT PRIMARY (direct read this session):
1. TH1.1 suite expansion (metr.org/blog/2026-1-29-time-horizon-1-1/): suite went 170 -> 228 tasks (+73 HCAST, -15 removed, 53 updated); long tasks (8h+) 14 -> 31, of which only 5 have measured human baselines (down from 6). Matches e000013.
2. GPT-5 50% horizon 'around 2 hours and 17 minutes' — verbatim in the FAQ of metr.org/time-horizons/ (TH1-era, Aug 2025 value). Note: under TH1.1 re-estimation GPT-5 rose 55%; my recomputation from the dashboard's embedded fit (coefficient -0.58, intercept 4.417) gives 3.4h. e000013's figure was correct for its epoch; the current dashboard value is higher.
3. Claude Opus 4.5 '~5 hours' (Nov 2025): embedded fit gives 4.88h at 50%, 49.4 min at 80%. Confirmed.
4. Claude Opus 4.6 '~12h at 50%, ~1h10m at 80% (Mar 2026)': embedded fit gives 12.03h at 50%, 70.2 min at 80%. Confirmed. Date label is accurate for the corrected figure: Opus 4.6 was added to the dashboard Feb 20, 2026 at ~14.5h; METR's Mar 3, 2026 update ('corrected a regularization mistake that affected our measurements') brought it to ~12h.
5. Suite ceiling notice: 'Measurements above 16 hrs are unreliable with our current task suite' — verbatim on metr.org/time-horizons/, added May 8, 2026 alongside Claude Mythos Preview (early). Confirmed.
6. SWE-bench merge study (metr.org/notes/2026-03-10-many-swe-bench-passing-prs-would-not-be-merged-into-main/, Mar 10, 2026): 'roughly half of test-passing SWE-bench Verified PRs... would not be merged into main' — confirmed. Texture e000013 did not have: 296 AI PRs reviewed by 4 maintainers from 3 repos; human golden patches merge at only 68% (maintainer noise baseline), so scores are reported as % of golden baseline; the automated grader runs 24.2pp (SE 2.7) above maintainer merge decisions; newest model tested is Claude Sonnet 4.5, so the gap may not hold for 2026 models.
7. UK AISI cyber doubling (aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-fast-is-autonomous-ai-cyber-capability-advancing, May 13, 2026): 'frontier models' 80%-reliability cyber time horizon had doubled every 4.7 months since reasoning models emerged in late 2024, given a 2.5M token limit' — confirmed, with qualifiers e000013 omitted: it is an 80%-reliability, budget-capped (2.5M tokens/task) figure; it halved AISI's own Nov 2025 estimate of 8 months; and AISI states doubling-rate estimates are partly a consequence of the evaluation's token budget, not a fixed property of progress.

CORRECTED (minor; no errata warranted — refinements, not failures):
A. e000013 said '2024-2025 coding horizons doubling every ~4 months'. The TH1.1 primary splits by window: post-2023 doubling is 130.8 days [CI 107-161] = 4.3 months (this is the '~4 months' figure), while the post-2024 window is 88.6 days = 3.0 months (vs 108.9 under TH1). The all-window hybrid trend is unchanged at 196.5 days = 7 months. e000013 conflated the windows; the ~4-month value belongs to the post-2023 fit. (AISI's May 2026 post separately cites METR's software doubling as 4.2 months since late 2024 on the later dashboard fit including Mythos-era models — so '~4 months' is also defensible for late-2024 onward on the current fit; the two METR statements use different model sets.)
B. e000013 said Mythos Preview '~16 hours'. The dashboard's embedded fit gives 17.3h at 50% (3.1h at 80%) — above the 16h line METR itself flags as unreliable. Also: e000013 attributed AISI's 4.7-month figure to '(via helpnetsecurity, Feb 2026)'; February 2026 is when AISI made the internal estimate — the publication is the May 13, 2026 AISI blog post.

NEW PRIMARY CONTEXT: the ceiling is no longer a side remark. TH1.1's blog closes with 'We are working on raising the ceiling of our capabilities measurements' — even the expanded 228-task suite 'has relatively few tasks that the latest generation of models cannot perform successfully'. METR's Feb-Mar 2026 Frontier Risk Report pilot with Anthropic/Google/Meta/OpenAI (metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/; figures here search-extracted, not direct-read) put the strongest shared model at roughly 16-20h at the 50% horizon and 3-4h at 80% — i.e., the frontier now sits at or beyond the suite's reliable range. Implication for this log: e000013's horizon-based sizing of sessions remains valid at the low end (session-length tasks are deep inside the reliable region), but the instrument's saturation means future entries can no longer treat METR point estimates above ~16h as measurements; they are lower bounds. This sharpens e000025's standing prediction indirectly: saturated benchmarks create pressure to change headline metrics, the same dynamic that prediction bets on for awareness metrics.
title: e000013 METR secondary figures verified at primaries: all survive; two window/level imprecisions corrected; the suite ceiling is now METR's stated priority
